meaning:
Γεννησαρέτ (Rec. Γενησ-, Mk, l.with; Targ. גְּנֵיסַר),
[in LXX: Γεννησάρ (as in some MSS. Mt, Mk), 1Ma.11:67 * ;]
Gennesaret, a fertile plain on W. shore of the Sea of Galilee; ἡ γῆ, Mat.14:34, Mrk.6:53; ἡ λίμνη (יָם כִּנֶּרֶת, Num.34:11, elsewhere ἡ θάλασσα τ. Γαλιλαίας, Mrk.1:16; ἡ θ. τ. Τιβεριάδος, Jhn.6:1), Luk.5:1.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: When they had crossed over, they came to the land of Gennesaret.
When they had crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret, and moored to the shore.
Now while the multitude pressed on him and heard the word of God, he was standing by the lake of Gennesaret.
